doc.title: Randy Brecker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 12, 2022

title: James Taylor's graph-paper horn charts
summary: James Taylor wrote horn parts on graph paper and the horn men transcribed them.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: You just never knew what kind of situation — I had another good one in mind, I’m trying to think of it now. Oh for instance — and these all ended up great records. James Taylor — we were close with him at one point, especially Barry was a close friend. And we did now I don’t know if I’ll remember the record. Of course Mike played on “Don’t Let me be Lonely Tonight” it had a wonderful tenor solo. “One Man Dog” it was an album. And James didn’t know traditional music writing or rhythms so he wrote the charts on graph paper where each horizontal line was a sixteenth note and each vertical line was a half step. And we had to sit there — but he actually spent all the time doing this. We spent hours transcribing and talking with him to get the charts. But it was amazing that he did it, he figured that out on his own as a way to communicate what he was looking for because he wanted specific horn parts.
